correctness.rationale: The statewise concurrence is derived from an explicitly reconstructed four-Kraus spin-flip matrix with 2x2 symmetric blocks and evaluated singular values; normalization and zero- and unit-visibility boundaries are specified. Haar measure is generated by four independent circular Gaussians; conditioning yields a complex-normal determinant, a gamma-two radius and an independent uniform beta ratio. Its exact Laplace integral is evaluated algebraically, and endpoint expansions follow from Taylor series. Direct spin-flip/PPT experiments (400 inputs), four integrals, three Haar frequencies and four endpoint checks agree; they corroborate but cannot replace the universal analytic proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A family-specific threshold does not cover positive-Haar-volume generic states with all four amplitudes. A statewise formula defines the integrand but obtaining the evaluated full Haar law requires an additional Gaussian-conditional and beta-gamma integration; this integration and resulting universal atom are the entire new claim. No analogous pure-dephasing Haar result implies an amplitude-damping ensemble formula: the channels are not equivalent under local basis changes and yield different limiting survival fractions.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The name sudden death is not itself new. Alternative formulations include the cumulative distribution of the damping threshold \(p=|ad-bc|/|d|^2\) (capped at 1), the Haar volume of PPT-negative output states and the time-to-separability survival function. Searches for these formulations and their arctangent constants found no explicit equivalent record; search failures alone are not evidence of uniqueness.

originality.rationale: The claim evaluated is the exact complex-Haar ensemble survival/lifetime distribution, not the well-known pointwise two-qubit sudden-death criterion. Inspected full-text primary literature addresses a two-component family, extended Werner family, noiseless Haar negativity or qualitative channel-state equivalence. Earlier broad arbitrary-state criteria are acknowledged and do imply the integrand once one adds nontrivial Haar geometry and integration, but do not state the completed arctangent law in available material. The inaccessible full texts leave genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: The full text of Jiang–Shi–Du (2011), which gives general statewise formulas, was unavailable; it could already evaluate a Haar ensemble or imply the displayed formula in an overlooked corollary.
The full text of Huang–Zhu (2007) was inaccessible; a relevant general volume or probability computation could appear beyond the abstract.
Semantic and public search coverage is finite. No independence of this result from all unindexed/unpublished literature is asserted.

value.rationale: It evaluates a natural full-Haar robustness distribution for a physically canonical channel, including exact full survival curve and finite-time death fraction \((6-\pi)/8\). The measure-theoretic transition differs from the known restricted-state thresholds and quantifies the experimentally meaningful nonuniformity of sudden death across randomly prepared pure states. This is a motivated new invariant, not an arbitrary finite grid/parameter slice, though it does not imply a general unequal-noise theorem.
